feedback: What I had to do in the controller: a wider track lowers effective steering gain by about 14 percent (0.12/0.14), so I raised kp from 0.8 to 0.93 to hold the iteration 3 gain. I kept kd at 0.15 and ki at 0 because no steady offset has appeared in any run (RMS 0.019 to 0.033 m) and the damping question is still open. The narrow-track evidence from iteration 4 (0.10 m, score 53.14, s-bend progress 0.156 to 0.081 with oscillation falling to 0.067) suggests that the robot is sluggish on bends when the track is narrow, so widening it is the right direction to test. Decision rules for the next race: if the score is above 69.18 and max_error falls toward 0.06 m with s-bend and slalom progress rising, keep wheel_track 0.14 m and move to the first requested change. If the score falls below 69.18 while oval progress drops (the tightest bend losing turn authority), return to wheel_track 0.12 m, since iteration 3 is the best known track. If steering_oscillation rises above the iteration 3 level (0.12 to 0.17) with max_error unchanged, the extra gain from kp 0.93 is the issue, so change kp in the controller, not the geometry.
requested_changes: If wheel_track 0.14 m raises the score above 69.18 and max_error falls, try wheel_radius 0.035 m with everything else unchanged. Iteration 3 progress was only 0.12 to 0.23 across tracks, far short of the full course, and a larger wheel gives more ground speed at the same PWM (a hypothesis from the progress shortfall, not yet measured).

If wheel_track 0.14 m drops oval progress below the iteration 3 level of about 0.23 while max_error is unchanged, return to wheel_track 0.12 m and try mass 0.7 kg alone. Iteration 1 (0.6 kg) cut oval oscillation to 0.074 but also cut progress, so mass 0.7 is a milder test of the same trade-off.

If line_loss_events on the slalom stay at 2.0 (iterations 0, 3 and 4) with max_error still above 0.06 m, try sensor_size 0.016 m at the 80 mm row as a single test. A larger footprint keeps the readings above the 0.05 line-loss threshold for longer. Iteration 1 changed sensor size together with other variables, so this effect is not yet proven.
